articles.title: NASA steps up work on nuclear-powered Mars mission - The New Indian Express
articles.content: NASA is advancing the development of a nuclear power system for its SR-1 Freedom spacecraft, which is scheduled to launch in late 2028 to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion beyond Earth’s orbit. The mission will mark the first time a fission-powered spacecraft travels beyond Earth orbit, paving the way for future deep-space exploration. NASA and its partners have agreed on key contract actions to accelerate development of the spacecraft’s nuclear power module and reduce technical risks. Sierra Lobo Inc. will develop the closed Brayton cycle power conversion system, which converts heat generated by a nuclear reactor into electricity. The system will provide electrical power for SR-1 Freedom’s propulsion demonstration and will be integrated with a fission reactor being developed by the US Department of Energy’s Idaho National Laboratory. The work will be carried out under a contract supporting spaceflight hardware development, testing and operations at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, Ohio. NASA and the Department of Energy are incorporating safety measures throughout the spacecraft’s development, including interagency reviews, regulatory compliance and assessments of potential hazards. The reactor will remain inactive until the spacecraft has left Earth orbit. SR-1 Freedom will also carry the SkyFall science mission, comprising three Mars helicopters developed from NASA’s Ingenuity design. The helicopters will collect scientific data, demonstrate exploration capabilities and identify potential water sources on Mars. The mission is expected to advance nuclear-powered technologies for future deep-space missions, including systems that could support NASA’s planned Moon base during extended periods of darkness or in locations with limited sunlight. articles.title: JEET AI Launches India's First AI Tutor That Goes Beyond Answers to Actually Teach
articles.content: Support our Journalism Depth, context and analysis Subscribe Home ANI Press Releases JEET AI Launches India's First AI Tutor That Goes Beyond Answers to... ANI Press Releases JEET AI Launches India’s First AI Tutor That Goes Beyond Answers to Actually Teach ANI PR 21 October, 2026 04:30 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Ritvik Kulshrestha, founder of JEET AI and CEO of Extramarks Education Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ PRNewswire New Delhi [India], October 21: JEET AI introduces India’s first AI Tutor that truly teaches, replicating the experience of learning with a personal teacher. Rather than waiting for students to ask questions, it actively teaches concepts, writes and annotates on a virtual board, presents relevant multimedia content, and uses interactive simulations to simplify complex topics. For instance, while teaching a concept in Chemistry, JEET AI can illustrate chemical reactions, explain the underlying science through visual demonstrations, and pause to test whether the student has understood the concept before moving forward. Show Full Article Just like a good teacher, it continuously checks comprehension, asks questions, and tests students throughout the lesson, adapting its explanations based on their understanding. Students can interrupt at any moment, ask unlimited questions, and request explanations repeatedly, without hesitation or judgment. JEET AI has launched with teaching capabilities in Hindi, with support for additional Indian languages, including Tamil and Kannada, set to be introduced in the coming months. For decades, students have relied on coaching centres, recorded lectures, and YouTube videos to prepare for their examinations. However, teaching hundreds of students simultaneously has made truly personalized learning nearly impossible. While personal tutoring offers individual attention, its high cost makes it inaccessible to most families. AI chatbots have made doubt solving easier than ever but answering questions and actually teaching are two very different things. JEET AI has set out to bridge this gap, bringing personalized teaching to students across India at a starting price of just ₹1,499 per month. Ritvik Kulshrestha, Founder of Jeet AI and CEO of Extramarks Education, said, “For centuries, the best form of education has been a great teacher sitting beside a student, understanding their difficulties, and adapting to their needs. Unfortunately, this level of personal attention has always been a privilege available to very few. With JEET AI, we are using technology to change that. Our goal is not to build another tool that answers questions, but to make the experience of having a great personal teacher accessible to every student.” Combining over 15 years of educational expertise, proprietary content, and pedagogical research from Extramarks Education, JEET AI goes beyond conventional AI tools to deliver an immersive, interactive learning experience that replicates a personalized one-on-one learning environment. Whether mastering a concept, learning an entire subject, or preparing for JEE or school examinations, JEET AI delivers structured, interactive, and personalized teaching, followed by targeted practice and comprehensive assessments to identify learning gaps and ensure thorough understanding and mastery of every concept. articles.title: Asian Granito unveils Dussehra campaign with TheSmallBigIdea - Adgully
articles.content: Asian Granito India Ltd. (AGL) has unveiled its Dussehra campaign, ‘Iss Dussehra, Soch Ko Thoda Premium Banao’, drawing inspiration from the festival’s celebration of the victory of good over evil to explore how everyday choices can shape the world around us. The film follows a young boy and a small cement Ravana that grows each time it witnesses acts of selfishness, from breaking traffic signals and cutting queues to littering and choosing anger over consideration. As people begin making more thoughtful choices, the Ravana starts to shrink. Using AI to transform the cement Ravana into a larger-than-life presence in real-world settings, the film brings the impact of everyday behaviour to life. Through this campaign, AGL takes its idea of ‘Premium’ beyond products and possessions, presenting it as a way of thinking and behaving. By encouraging people to make choices that reflect consideration, responsibility and thoughtfulness, the campaign brings the spirit of Dussehra into everyday life, highlighting how small, positive actions can contribute to a better world. articles.title: AI -Powered Sorting Technology Targets Quality and Labour Challenges in the Arecanut Industry
articles.content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering India’s arecanut supply chain, with an Indian startup introducing an optical sorting system designed to improve quality inspection, processing efficiency and automation. Agrograde, which develops AI and physical automation technologies for agricultural supply chains, has installed its first commercial arecanut sorting system at Vikas Traders in Mangalore, Karnataka. The system can process approximately one tonne of arecanut per hour, enabling the Mangalore facility to process close to eight tonnes a day. It uses computer vision and AI to inspect individual nuts, identify defects and automatically separate rejected material from accepted produce. The technology targets a longstanding challenge in the arecanut trade: maintaining consistent quality while processing large volumes. Unlike conventional colour-sorting machines, which primarily identify differences in colour, Agrograde’s system is designed to detect external defects that may not be distinguishable through colour alone. The system uses Agrograde’s patent-pending Vector technology to capture 10–12 images of each nut. Proprietary AI models analyse these images within milliseconds, identify visible defects and guide the mechanism that separates rejected nuts from the accepted lot. The models have been trained using hundreds of thousands of crop images and run on high-performance computing infrastructure powered by NVIDIA. Rakeshkumar Barai, Co-Founder of Agrograde, said the company studies crop characteristics, including how produce rolls and glides, variations in size and shape, dust levels, and the force required for gentle sorting. He said developing the arecanut sorter took almost five months and three product iterations, with research focused on existing quality-assessment practices and the crop’s specific requirements. “This AI sorter has made warehouse operations almost completely autonomous,” he said. The machine is based on Agrograde’s Vector architecture, which ensures high surface coverage as an object moves through the vision system. It is also designed to handle considerable variations in the size and shape of produce. Aniket Ghadage, Head of Product Engineering at Agrograde, said the Vector architecture follows a design philosophy that makes sophisticated machines easier to operate and maintain. It is also designed to function in challenging environmental conditions, including heat, dust and humidity. Agrograde developed the system in collaboration with Vikas Traders, a Mangalore-based agribusiness with decades of experience in the arecanut trade. The partnership helped adapt the technology to actual warehouse conditions, including dust, foreign matter and high humidity. When initially commissioned, the system recorded approximately 75% sorting accuracy. Following updates to its AI models using commercial operating data, accuracy increased to around 89%. The company expects further improvements as additional data becomes available. Before automation, Vikas Traders depended heavily on manual inspection. According to the company, one worker could sort roughly two bags a day, while a team of around 15 people processed approximately 40–45 bags daily. The availability of skilled labour also affected inspection, packing and dispatch schedules. The automated system provides more predictable processing capacity and generates a quality report for every lot, covering size distribution, identified defects, defect intensity and the number of nuts packed. articles.title: The Aditya-L1 Mission - INSIGHTS IAS - Simplifying UPSC IAS Exam Preparation
articles.content: Source: TH Subject: Science and Technology Context: Scientists at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) developed Doppler velocity images of the solar corona using data from the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) payload onboard India’s maiden solar mission, Aditya-L1. The Aditya-L1 Mission About The Aditya-L1 Mission : What it is? India’s first dedicated space-based observatory mission designed to continuously observe the Sun’s outermost layers—the photosphere, chromosphere, and corona—as well as measure solar wind and local magnetic fields . Organisation: Developed and operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Timeline: Launch Date: September 2, 2023 (aboard PSLV-C57 from SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota). Halo-Orbit Insertion (HOI): Successfully inserted into its targeted halo orbit around the Sun–Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1) on January 6, 2024 . Operational Mission Life: Designed for an active observing mission lifespan of 5 years. Aim: To investigate coronal heating, solar flare formation, coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and space weather processes influencing Earth’s magnetosphere and the interplanetary environment. Key Features of the Mission: Continuous Observation from L1: Positioned approximately 1.5 million km from Earth near the Sun–Earth Lagrange Point 1 , enabling uninterrupted solar observations without eclipses. Seven Scientific Payloads: Carries four remote-sensing instruments (VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS) and three in-situ instruments (ASPEX, PAPA and magnetometers) for comprehensive solar studies. Multi-Layered Solar Observations: Studies the photosphere, chromosphere and corona through electromagnetic radiation, energetic particles and magnetic field measurements, revealing interconnected solar processes. Space Weather Monitoring : Tracks solar wind, coronal mass ejections and magnetic disturbances, improving understanding and forecasting of space weather threats to Earth. Recent Discovery: Doppler Velocity Imaging of the Corona Tracking Coronal Mass Ejections: Captured Doppler velocity images of the solar corona, helping determine whether erupting plasma moves toward Earth or travels elsewhere in space. Application of Doppler Effect : Uses wavelength shifts in sunlight, where positive velocities indicate plasma moving away and negative velocities indicate movement toward the observer. Visible Spectroscopy Capability: The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) enables specialized visible-light spectroscopy, producing detailed coronal plasma velocity maps for studying solar eruptions.

articles.title: Pujara Backs Bhuvneshwar As India's First -Choice New-Ball Bowler in New Zealand
articles.content: Pujara Backs Bhuvneshwar As India's First-Choice New-Ball Bowler in New Zealand Bhuvneshwar's ability to exploit movement in the air and off the pitch makes him suited for the conditions in New Zealand, where Shreyas Iyer will look to secure a series victory under his captaincy By : PTI Update: 2026-10-21 09:25 GMT India's Bhuvneshwar Kumar. New Delhi: Cheteshwar Pujara believes Bhuvneshwar Kumar should be India's first-choice new-ball bowler in New Zealand, as the conditions Down Under would be ideal for the experienced pacer's swing bowling. Bhuvneshwar's ability to exploit movement in the air and off the pitch makes him suited for the conditions in New Zealand, where Shreyas Iyer will look to secure a series victory under his captaincy. The five-match series begins on Thursday in Christchurch. "In New Zealand, he should be the first choice with the new ball, based on the conditions, because of the skill he possesses of swinging the ball. If the ball won't swing in New Zealand, where else will it swing? The conditions there are ideal for him," Pujara said on JioHotstar's 'Out or Not Out'. "If there is a little help from the pitch, he can extract that movement from the pitch very well with the new ball," he added. Pujara also said that a victory in New Zealand would provide a significant confidence boost to both the captain and the team, given the challenges of performing in overseas conditions. "When you go to New Zealand and defeat the New Zealand team, it's a big achievement. Performing well in overseas conditions for the Indian team in any format, whether it is ODIs, T20Is, or a Test match, boosts your confidence," he said. "If you do well there as a captain or as a team, your confidence goes up, that you can perform well not just in Indian conditions, but anywhere in the world." Former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar pointed out that Bhuvneshwar has excelled in the IPL despite the absence of seam-friendly conditions, bowling both with the new ball and at the death over the last two seasons. "In the IPL, there aren't seaming conditions, there are flat pitches. Yet, for two years, he has been bowling two overs at the top and two at the back end, the toughest phases of the game," Nayar said. "To do that, you need experience, you need a bowler who understands the conditions and can extract the best out of those conditions, and there has never been a question about Bhuvneshwar Kumar." Nayar said he was pleased to see the experienced pacer return to the national set-up. Nayar also said that success in New Zealand would help Iyer establish his credentials as a captain, particularly given the comparisons with Suryakumar Yadav, who previously led India in T20Is.
